chunks.chunk_summary: This chunk contains information about the definition, alternative names, valuation rationale, and market characteristics of option time value in finance.
chunks.page_content: A rational investor pays the time value (TV) of an option based on the probability the option will increase in value before expiry. The time value (TV) can be thought of as the "risk premium" the option seller charges the buyer. The time value (TV) can be thought of as the price an investor is willing to pay for potential upside. In finance, the time value (TV) of an option is also known as "extrinsic" or "instrumental" value. An American option is always worth more than its current exercise value in a fair market. For an American option, the time value (TV) is always greater than zero in a fair market. The time value (TV) of an option is the premium a rational investor would pay over its current exercise value (intrinsic value).

chunks.page_content: Minority discount is an economic concept. Minority ownership limits the scope of control over critical aspects of the business. Ownership of a 51% share in the business is usually worth more than 51% of its equity value. Share prices of public companies usually reflect the minority discount. The concept of minority discount applies to equities with voting power. Ownership of a 30% share in the business may be worth less than 30% of its equity value. The phenomenon where ownership of a 51% share in the business is worth more than 51% of its equity value is called the premium for control. Minority discount reflects the notion that a partial ownership interest may be worth less than its proportional share of the total business.

chunks.chunk_summary: This chunk contains information about the forward premium anomaly (also known as the forward premium puzzle or Fama puzzle) in currency markets, including its definition, empirical findings regarding interest rate differentials and currency appreciation, theoretical expectations of investor behavior under equal risk conditions, and related hypotheses such as the Unbiasedness hypothesis.
chunks.page_content: The forward premium anomaly in currency markets is also referred to as the forward premium puzzle. Economic theory suggests that if all currencies are equally risky investors would demand higher interest rates on currencies expected to fall in value. The forward premium anomaly refers to the well documented empirical finding that the domestic currency is expected to appreciate when domestic nominal interest rates exceed foreign interest rates. There is a hypothesis called the Unbiasedness hypothesis related to the Forward exchange rate. The finding that the domestic currency is expected to appreciate when domestic nominal interest rates exceed foreign interest rates is puzzling because economic theory suggests that if all currencies are equally risky investors would demand higher interest rates on currencies expected to fall in value. The forward premium anomaly in currency markets is also referred to as the Fama puzzle.
